resources.string: Own screen adds a tablet-sized screen to the computer, which makes its monitors flicker once. Auto uses it only when the computer is locked, so nobody at the desk is disturbed, and otherwise mirrors the monitor closest to the tablet\'s shape without changing it.
Ask for fingerprint or PIN to connect
Connecting unlocks the computer, so whoever holds the unlocked tablet must prove it is theirs first.
This tablet has no screen lock, so there is nothing to ask for. Set one up in Android\'s settings to use this.
Stop asking for fingerprint or PIN
Not paired. Run desklinkd pair on the computer, then tap Pair to scan its QR code.

Timed out: asleep, or not reachable from this network
This tests only HTTPS, on port %1$d; the stream\'s UDP is not tested yet.
Top bar and overview here until you disconnect
Every window moves here; they go back when the desk turns on
So a job left running goes on; ∞ lasts until you connect again. The desk still locks.
Sends Win, Win+key and Alt+Tab to your computer while DeskLink shows it

Android keeps Win, every Win+key combination and Alt+Tab for itself, so DeskLink cannot pass them to your computer. With this on, DeskLink receives the physical keyboard\'s keys first, but only takes them while a DeskLink session is on screen; at any other time every key goes to Android as usual. It reads no screen content and sends keys only to the computer you connected to.
On: Win, Win+key and Alt+Tab go to the computer.

Off: Android keeps these keys. Turn on "DeskLink keyboard shortcuts" in the accessibility settings. If Android says the setting is restricted, open DeskLink\'s App info, tap ⋮ and allow restricted settings first.
